messages:
ana: quick flag: replay harness long-prefill run shows a nontrivial perf drop after landing the kv-prefill heuristic + new kernel hint changes. rough numbers below.

mike_r: ok can you paste the exact invocation and the commit you started from? we need an apples-to-apples repro.

ana: starting point: main@c9f3a2 -> bisect -> runtime/kv-prefill-heuristics@f1b2. replay run:
```
./harness/replay --model redwood-v2-8k --seed 42 --seqlen 8192 --prefill=true \
  --batch_policy adaptive --adaptive_threshold 0.7 --kv_shards 1 \
  --kernel_hint matmul_fused_epyc
```
perf summary snippet: 
```
prefill_tokens: 6.5M
tokens/sec: 43.2 (this run)
baseline tokens/sec: 52.6 (master last week)
95p latency: 220ms -> 310ms
```

cheng: is that the canonical longctx-prefill-trace v3 we use for customer A? verify input hashes + tokenizer versions please.

ana: yes v3 trace from testdata/longctx_traces/v3, input sha256 3a7d... tokenizer v2.1, weights pinned to release-2026-02-12.

perf-bot: Regression alert: longctx-prefill v3 tokens/sec -17.9% vs baseline. see https://perf.redwood/test/2012345678

mike_r: two hypotheses: (1) adaptive batching threshold causes switch to large-batch kernel shapes that are suboptimal for heavy-prefill shapes, (2) fused kernel hint changes memory access stride and hurts KV prefetch. run microprof.

cheng: run microprof with counters during the replay window: cycles, L1/L2 misses, mem-loads. use tools/microprof and attach to runtime pid.

ana: microprof results (aggregated per-token during prefill window):
- matmul stage cycles/token +12%
- KV apply mem-loads/token +30%
- L2 miss rate 6.2% -> 11.8%

lucy: that's a memory-locality issue. did the heuristic change KV shard placement or replication?

ana: kv-prefill-heuristics introduces kv_shard_preference with default prefer_local when adaptive_batch fires. combined with matmul_fused it looks like page residency changed.

mike_r: run controlled variants: (A) prefer_local=false, (B) kernel_hint=matmul_basic (old). keep seeds and all else identical.

ana: results: (A) tokens/sec 50.8, (B) tokens/sec 51.2, baseline ~52.6. so reverting either knob recovers most perf. together they regress.

cheng: conclusion: interaction bug between kv placement heuristic and fused matmul kernel memory pattern. fused kernel changes stride/prefetch expectations so prefer_local ends up incurring more cross-device memory ops.

lucy: docs/process note: add explicit isolation rule to bench methodology: when testing kernel swaps, freeze KV placement/replication unless testing placement. also add microprof stage to replay recipe.

mike_r: action items:
- ana: revert default to prefer_remote (or neutral) and add a canary flag to opt-in prefer_local. include repro script + perf dump in PR. due EOD.
- cheng: add microprof collector stage to replay harness emitting per-kernel L1/L2 miss counters and cycles. due tomorrow.
- lucy: update eng-runtime benchmark methodology checklist to include kv-vs-kernel isolation and microprof step. due EOD.

ana: PR opened: runtime PR#784 (revert + canary). includes short unit test that runs a 1k-prefill workload with both kernel hints to catch regressions.

perf-bot: CI perf run for PR#784: longctx-prefill v3 delta +0.5% (within noise). details: https://perf.redwood/pr/784

mike_r: good. also add a tiny synthetic microbenchmark that stresses sequential KV hits (no batching) to run in nightly kernel validation. helps catch prefetch regressions.

cheng: i'll add that microbenchmark and wire it into nightly. lucy please add the postmortem note to eng-runtime/team-docs/bench-notes.md summarizing root cause and how to avoid.

lucy: done, note added with repro steps and mitigation.

ana: TL;DR: perf regression caused by interaction between new kv prefer_local default + fused matmul kernel. revert default, add canary, add microprofiling to harness, add microbenchmark and docs. PR mitigates and CI confirms. :party_parrot:

mike_r: excellent triage. follow-up: test on Dedicated multi-GPU KV sharding next week and close loop with customer A.
